name: current_network
summary: Report this Mac's place on the network: active interface, IPv4 address, this device's MAC, subnet mask, subnet host capacity, and the default gateway/router IP. Use first when diagnosing connectivity — it tells you who you are and which router to test against.

name: dns_servers
summary: List the DNS resolver IPs this Mac is using. Useful when a host pings by IP but names won't resolve — that points at DNS rather than the link.

name: ping_host
summary: Ping a host (IP or hostname) to test reachability; reports packet loss and round-trip time. To diagnose 'no internet', ping the gateway from current_network, then a public IP such as 8.8.8.8.

params.name: host
params.description: IP or hostname to ping. Bare host only (e.g. 8.8.8.8, router.local, apple.com); option-like or punctuated values are rejected.

params.name: count
params.description: How many echo requests to send (1–10, default 3).

name: dns_lookup
summary: Resolve a hostname to its IPs (A/AAAA), or reverse-resolve an IP to its hostname (PTR). Use to confirm DNS is working when names fail but IPs succeed.

params.name: host
params.description: Hostname to resolve (e.g. apple.com) or an IP to reverse-resolve (e.g. 17.253.144.10). Bare host only; option-like or punctuated values are rejected.

name: listening_ports
summary: List the ports this Mac is listening on and which process (name + PID) owns each. Answers 'what's using port N' and 'what's accepting connections on this machine'.

params.name: protocol
params.description: Transport to report: tcp (default), udp, or both.

name: lan_devices
summary: List other devices on the LAN (IP + MAC) from this Mac's ARP cache. Only shows hosts this Mac has recently talked to, not every device — use scan_lan for a fuller sweep.

name: scan_lan
summary: Actively discover LAN devices by pinging every address in this Mac's IPv4 subnet, then reporting the IP + MAC of every host that answered. Fuller than lan_devices but slower and it generates traffic, so choose it deliberately. /24-or-smaller subnets only, bounded by the request timeout.

name: trace_route
summary: Trace the network path to a host, listing every router (hop) between this Mac and the destination with the round-trip time to each. Use it to find WHERE a connection breaks or slows down: a hop that stops responding or spikes in latency localizes the problem far beyond a plain ping (which only says reachable / not reachable).

params.name: host
params.description: IP or hostname to trace the route to (e.g. 8.8.8.8, apple.com). Bare host only; option-like or punctuated values are rejected.

params.name: max_hops
params.description: Maximum number of hops (routers) to probe before giving up (1–30, default 15). Lower finishes faster; raise it only for a distant host that legitimately needs more than 15 hops.

name: whois_lookup
summary: Look up the WHOIS registration record for a domain or IP — who owns it, the registrar, and the create/expiry dates. Answers 'who owns this domain' and 'when does it expire'.

params.name: domain
params.description: Domain name (e.g. apple.com) or IP address to look up. Bare host only; option-like or punctuated values are rejected.

name: route_table
summary: Show this Mac's kernel routing table (IPv4 and IPv6): which gateway and interface each destination network is reached through. Use it to confirm the default route and spot a stray or VPN-added route that is sending traffic the wrong way.

name: interface_stats
summary: Report per-interface traffic counters (packets in/out and errors) for every network interface. Use it to see which interface is actually carrying traffic and whether an interface is logging errors or drops.

name: dns_cache_lookup
summary: Resolve a hostname through macOS's directory-services layer (dscacheutil), the same path apps use. Complements dns_lookup (which queries DNS directly with dig): comparing the two shows whether a name is being served from a local cache/override rather than fresh DNS.

params.name: host
params.description: Hostname to resolve through directory services (e.g. apple.com). Bare host only; option-like or punctuated values are rejected.

name: flush_dns_cache
summary: Flush this Mac's directory-services DNS cache so the next name lookups resolve fresh. Use it after changing DNS servers or when a hostname is resolving to a stale IP. Benign and runs immediately (the cache simply repopulates on demand). Note: this clears dscacheutil's cache only — a full mDNSResponder reset needs administrator rights and is out of scope.
